# Alopex

> Alopex is an open-source (MIT), self-hosted net worth tracker for people with European bank accounts. It syncs balances and transactions read-only from 2000+ banks over PSD2 (via Enable Banking), prices stocks and crypto, and stores everything in the user's own Supabase project. There is no Alopex server: the publisher never sees user data.

Key facts:
- License: MIT. Author: Marco D'Onghia.
- Bank sync: PSD2 account information (read-only) via Enable Banking, 2000+ European banks (e.g. Revolut, Wise, Fineco). Syncs every 6 hours. Consent lasts 180 days. No US/Canadian banks.
- Investments: holdings entered by the user, priced via Yahoo Finance; crypto via CoinGecko and a read-only Coinbase key.
- Currencies: EUR, USD or GBP, daily ECB rates.
- Categorization: user rules first, optional Google Gemini for the rest.
- Also: Splitwise shared costs, reports, income vs expenses, subscription detection, transfer and refund pairing, "worth it?" Web Push prompts, installable PWA, CSV import.
- Hosting: runs on the user's own Supabase and Vercel (free tiers), or Docker. Setup: one command, `npx create-alopex` (Node 20+), about 30 minutes including the Enable Banking signup. Sync runs on pg_cron inside the user's Supabase project.
- Not included: budgets, savings goals, forecasts, broker sync.
- Not financial advice.

## Compared with
| | Alopex | Monarch Money | Finary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price | Free (MIT) | $99.99/year | Free for 2 accounts, paid from €54.99/year |
| European banks | 2000+ over PSD2 | No (US and Canada) | Yes |
| Where data lives | User's own Supabase | Monarch servers | Finary servers |
| Open source | Yes | No | No |
Prices checked 2026-11-09: https://www.monarchmoney.com/pricing , https://finary.com/en/pricing

## FAQ
- Is there an open-source alternative to Monarch Money for European banks? Yes: Alopex, MIT-licensed and self-hosted, with PSD2 sync for 2000+ European banks.
- Is it free? Yes. It runs on the free tiers of Supabase, Vercel and Enable Banking. The trade-off is that the user hosts it and renews bank consent every 180 days.
- How long does bank access last? 180 days of PSD2 consent (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/2360), then a one-click renewal without losing history.
- Can it move money? No. Access is read-only.
